summary: Korean stocks are in a bear market. The KOSPI fell 7.57% to 5,554.22 on Oct 15, its seventh straight loss and lowest close since April 7, tripping a sidecar and a Level 1 circuit breaker; Korea Times puts it about 40% below its June 19 peak of 9,385. SK hynix fell about 11% and Samsung about 9.5% on doubts about AI returns, a possible memory glut from China's CXMT, and the chance of another US rate hike. Server DRAM spot prices are still rising, so the stocks are falling faster than the business. The Bank of Korea raised its rate to 3.0% in August and meets Oct 22; SK hynix reports Oct 28 and Samsung Oct 29. Samsung and SK hynix have no regular US listing, so US investors reach Korea mostly through EWY, Korean bank ADRs and Coupang. On Oct 16 the index bounced: about 2.1% to 5,668.05 early (AP) and about 4.1% to 5,782.62 in a later Saxo update; the close was not confirmed at writing. The Oct 16 close was 5,668.06, up 2.05%, but the KOSPI lost 14.46% for the week, its worst week since October 2008. Surveys published Oct 18 expect the Bank of Korea to hold at 3.00% on Oct 22 and hike in November.
for_you: Korea is a memory chip market, and memory is breaking down. Skip MU and memory swings until the selling stops. Avoid new buys in Korean bank ADRs before the Oct 22 Bank of Korea decision.

changes.what: The KOSPI fell 2.62% to about 6,626 as foreigners kept selling Samsung and SK Hynix, each down about 2.4%. Profit taking in memory chips is driving Korea lower.

The KOSPI fell 3.65% to 6,384.24, its lowest close since Aug 11, as foreigners sold a net 2.02 trillion won for a tenth straight day. Samsung fell 4.39% and SK Hynix 4.52%, and China's CXMT said a new memory platform is in mass production.
changes.for_you: No action. Korean bank ADRs fall with foreign outflows; avoid new buys before the Oct 22 Bank of Korea decision. The same memory selloff hit MU premarket, so skip memory swings for now.

changes.what: The KOSPI fell about 6% on Oct 13, below 6,000 for the first time since August, and a sell sidecar paused program selling. SK Hynix fell about 8.5% and Samsung about 6.8%, with SK Square down about 12%.
changes.for_you: No action except to stay out. EWY fell 4% Monday and has more to digest; MU is not a setup. Watch the Oct 22 Bank of Korea decision.

changes.what: Correction and update: the KOSPI closed Oct 13 at 6,035.35, down 5.46%, not below 6,000 (that was intraday). SK Hynix closed down 10.09% and Samsung 7.39%. On Oct 14 an early rebound of over 2% faded and the index closed down 0.44% at 6,008.81, its sixth straight loss, with Samsung up 0.65% and SK Hynix down 1.66%.
changes.for_you: No action. A failed bounce is a sign the selling is not done, so no MU or memory swings. KB, SHG and WF stay hurt; watch the Oct 22 Bank of Korea decision.

changes.what: The KOSPI plunged 7.57% to 5,554.22 on Oct 15 ('Black Thursday'), its seventh straight loss, with a sell side sidecar at 9:07am and a Level 1 circuit breaker at 12:38pm. SK hynix fell about 11% to 1,262,000 won and Samsung about 9.5% to 210,000 won. Analysts cited AI return doubts, China's CXMT and US rate hike risk.
changes.for_you: No action. Do not sell puts on EWY or MU into this; rich premiums reflect real risk. Korean banks stay hurt into the Oct 22 Bank of Korea decision. CPNG is left out because its business is retail, not chips.

changes.what: The KOSPI bounced on Oct 16 after the 7.57% crash: AP had it up about 2.1% at 5,668.05 early, and Saxo later reported a 4.11% gain to 5,782.62, with Samsung and SK hynix steadying. The close was not confirmed at writing.
changes.for_you: No action. One up day after a 7.6% crash is not a bottom, so EWY and MU are in neither list. Wait for SK hynix (Oct 28) and Samsung (Oct 29) results before any memory trade. EWY closed Oct 15 at 156.22, down 11% in a month.

changes.what: The KOSPI closed Oct 16 up 2.05% at 5,668.06 but lost 14.46% for the week, its biggest weekly drop since October 2008 (TradingKey). Samsung closed at 215,500 won (up 2.62%) and SK hynix at 1,272,000 won (up 0.79%). In New York EWY fell 3.7% to 150.44 the same day as US chip stocks sold off again (dashboard).
changes.for_you: No action. A 14% week is forced selling; wait for SK hynix on Oct 28 before any Korea or memory trade. Korean bank ADRs stay hurt into the Oct 22 Bank of Korea decision. CPNG is left out: its business is retail, not chips.

changes.what: Two surveys published Oct 18 expect the Bank of Korea to hold its 3.00% rate on Oct 22: 19 of 20 experts in a Seoul Economic Daily poll and all 11 in a MoneyToday poll. Most expect a 'hawkish hold' and another hike in November, sooner if the Fed signals a December hike.
changes.for_you: No action. A hold removes Thursday's surprise risk, but a November hike stays on the table, so Korean bank ADRs (KB 118.81, SHG 70.31) stay hurt. Wait for SK hynix on Oct 28 before any Korea or memory trade.
